summary_out.hypothesis: L5's next text identified the spread-tight guard as the highest-leverage genuinely-orthogonal candidate beyond the (adverse, age) conjunction. The mechanism: spread is a fill-cost axis, not a signal-direction axis -- an adverse-rich aged reversal can still be expensive to enter if the book is thin right then, because crossing a wide spread to flip pays the mid-edge away to the spread-crossing cost. I chose the strictest 1-tick threshold (= the MES minimum) on the reasoning that this maximally tests the orthogonality hypothesis -- if 1 tick is too strict, pnl regresses while trade_count drops materially below base, an unambiguous diagnostic for L7. Predicted +$50 to +$150 pnl gain on -50 to -250 trade drop. STRONGLY VINDICATED: trade_count drop landed at the predicted -286 boundary, pnl gain was +$272 (80% to 440% above the predicted bracket). Crucially, this means the spread guard was binding on admits that the (adverse, age) conjunction was NOT already filtering -- ruling out the explicit failure mode the hypothesis bet against (that spread correlates with adverse-mid at admit time).
summary_out.brief_summary: ptg-b-l6 (position-tier-gate brief-summary loop 6) added a tight-spread guard (current_spread <= 1 tick) as a CONJUNCTION with L5's (adverse >= 5 ticks AND age >= 5s). Result: PASS vs simple (+7983.82% pnl) and dramatic closing of the gap to base (-9.54% -> -1.91% vs base, +7.6 pp). Still WORSE than base on 10/11 dates, exact parity on 1/11; aggregate gap shrunk to -$68 over 11 dates (avg -$6/date). vs L5: +$272 pnl (+8.43%) on -286 trades (-0.39%); 10/11 dates improved over L5, 1/11 unchanged -- the most consistent loop in the lineage. The spread axis is demonstrated to be GENUINELY orthogonal to (adverse, age): the +$272 gain came from filtering admits that the first two filters silently let through (wide-spread reversal flips). Lineage trajectory now L1->L6: -75.33%, -41.30%, -22.29%, -11.88%, -9.54%, -1.91% vs base. Marginal pnl per loop: $1213, $677, $371, $83.50, $272 -- L6 broke the diminishing-returns pattern decisively.
summary_out.next: Two natural directions for L7. (i) ONE more orthogonal structural conditioner -- the residual $68 gap is small but consistent (worse on 10/11 dates). The most genuinely orthogonal remaining candidate is signed aggressor flow: admit the reversal only if the most recent N trades (e.g. last 1 second of trade messages) show aggressor flow agreeing with the proposed NEW direction. This is a flow-confirmation axis, mathematically distinct from price displacement (adverse-mid), time (age), and quote thickness (spread). Predicted endpoint: tiny pnl drift (+$0 to +$50) -- the residual gap is so small that any new filter risks throwing out beneficial admits in addition to losers, and aggressor flow is itself partially correlated with adverse-mid because losing positions are by definition on the side aggressors are NOT hitting. (ii) Tune an existing knob -- relax spread to 2 ticks since at 1 tick the guard binds on ~286 trades and a slightly looser guard may capture +$5 to +$30 of admits that lose only a fraction of a tick on average. Pick (i) -- aggressor flow -- because it directly addresses the L7 question 'can a new orthogonal axis cross over base?' and (ii) is a single-axis sweep on a near-saturated knob with negligible expected upside. For aggressor-flow lookback window, choose 1 second (matches L5's age scale, balances signal smoothing against staleness on 30s oracle horizon); for agreement threshold, choose >= 60% same-side aggressor volume (modest majority, not a supermajority that would collapse to zero admits). In-flight diagnostic: if L7 pnl regresses with trade_count dropping below base, aggressor majority is correlated with adverse-mid and L8 should pivot to (ii) loosen spread to 2 ticks. If L7 pnl is flat with trade_count within +/-0.5% of L6, aggressor adds zero -- L8 should stop adding conjunctions and instead either tune existing knobs or accept that the 8-loop arm has saturated. If L7 crosses base, L8 should freeze L7 and add no further conditioner.
